summary: This upgrade from Kubernetes 1.23 to 1.29 spans six minor versions and introduces multiple critical breaking changes requiring immediate action. The most severe risks include complete removal of PodSecurityPolicy (requiring migration to Pod Security Admission), dockershim removal (requiring container runtime migration to containerd/CRI-O), and removal of 10+ deprecated API versions including CronJob v1beta1, HorizontalPodAutoscaler v2beta1/v2beta2, EndpointSlice v1beta1, Event v1beta1, and PodDisruptionBudget v1beta1—all of which will cause application failures if manifests or API clients haven't been updated. Additionally, the default behavior change for service account token auto-generation and kubeadm's new super-admin.conf separation will break existing automation expecting legacy behavior.

risk_paths.path_name: FlowSchema and PriorityLevelConfiguration v1beta2 API removed
risk_paths.description: The flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta2 API version of FlowSchema and PriorityLevelConfiguration is no longer served as of v1.29. Applications or tools that reference these API versions in manifests or API clients will fail.

conditions.statement: Target Kubernetes version is 1.29 or higher

evidence.quote_or_summary: The flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta2 API version of FlowSchema and PriorityLevelConfiguration is no longer served as of v1.29.

conditions.statement: Application manifests or API clients reference flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta2 API version

evidence.quote_or_summary: Migrate manifests and API clients to use the flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1 API version, available since v1.29, or the flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta3 API version, available since v1.26.
evidence.relevance: Specifies that manifests and API clients need migration

suggested_actions: Grep manifests for 'apiVersion: flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta2'
Search code for references to 'flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta2'
Migrate to flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1 or v1beta3 API versions before upgrading to 1.29
Note that spec.limited.assuredConcurrencyShares is renamed to spec.limited.nominalConcurrencyShares in v1

risk_paths.path_name: EndpointSlice v1beta1 API removed with field changes
risk_paths.description: The discovery.k8s.io/v1beta1 API version of EndpointSlice is no longer served as of v1.25. The v1 version has breaking changes including replacement of topology field with deprecatedTopology (not writable), and per-endpoint nodeName and zone fields.

conditions.statement: Target Kubernetes version is 1.25 or higher (upgrade to 1.29 includes this)

evidence.quote_or_summary: The discovery.k8s.io/v1beta1 API version of EndpointSlice is no longer served as of v1.25.

Search code for references to 'discovery.k8s.io/v1beta1' EndpointSlice
Migrate to discovery.k8s.io/v1 API version before upgrading to 1.25+
Replace topology["kubernetes.io/hostname"] with per-endpoint nodeName field
Replace topology["topology.kubernetes.io/zone"] with per-endpoint zone field

risk_paths.description: The events.k8s.io/v1beta1 API version of Event is no longer served as of v1.25. The v1 version has multiple breaking changes including renamed fields (involvedObject to regarding), new required fields, and deprecated timestamp/count fields not permitted in new v1 Events.

conditions.statement: Target Kubernetes version is 1.25 or higher (upgrade to 1.29 includes this)

evidence.quote_or_summary: The events.k8s.io/v1beta1 API version of Event is no longer served as of v1.25.

conditions.statement: Application code creates or updates events.k8s.io/v1beta1 Event objects

evidence.quote_or_summary: Migrate manifests and API clients to use the events.k8s.io/v1 API version, available since v1.19.
evidence.relevance: Specifies that manifests and API clients need migration

suggested_actions: Grep manifests for 'apiVersion: events.k8s.io/v1beta1' with 'kind: Event'
Search code for references to 'events.k8s.io/v1beta1' Event
Migrate to events.k8s.io/v1 API version before upgrading to 1.25+
Update involvedObject field to regarding
Ensure action, reason, reportingController, and reportingInstance are provided when creating events
Replace firstTimestamp with eventTime, lastTimestamp with series.lastObservedTime, count with series.count
Replace source.component with reportingController and source.host with reportingInstance

Migrate to policy/v1 API version before upgrading to 1.25+

risk_paths.description: PodSecurityPolicy in the policy/v1beta1 API version is no longer served as of v1.25, and the PodSecurityPolicy admission controller is removed. Pods will no longer be validated or mutated by PSPs after upgrade.

conditions.statement: Target Kubernetes version is 1.25 or higher (upgrade to 1.29 includes this)

evidence.quote_or_summary: PodSecurityPolicy in the policy/v1beta1 API version is no longer served as of v1.25, and the PodSecurityPolicy admission controller will be removed.

conditions.statement: Cluster has PodSecurityPolicy objects or relies on PSP admission controller

evidence.quote_or_summary: Migrate to Pod Security Admission or a 3rd party admission webhook. For a migration guide, see Migrate from PodSecurityPolicy to the Built-In PodSecurity Admission Controller.

suggested_actions: List all PodSecurityPolicy objects in the cluster: kubectl get psp
Identify workloads relying on PSP for security constraints
Migrate to Pod Security Admission (PSA) or 3rd party admission webhooks before upgrading to 1.25+
Follow migration guide: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/migrate-from-psp/
Test PSA configuration in audit/warn mode before enforcing

risk_paths.description: Docker runtime support using dockershim in the kubelet is completely removed in 1.24. Clusters using Docker as the container runtime will fail unless migrated to a CRI-compliant runtime (containerd, CRI-O) or cri-dockerd.

conditions.statement: Target Kubernetes version is 1.24 or higher (upgrade to 1.29 includes this)

evidence.quote_or_summary: Docker runtime support using dockershim in the kubelet is now completely removed in 1.24.

conditions.statement: Kubelet is configured to use Docker as container runtime (via dockershim)

evidence.quote_or_summary: From v1.24 onwards, you will need to either use one of the other supported runtimes (such as containerd or CRI-O) or use cri-dockerd if you are relying on Docker Engine as your container runtime.

suggested_actions: Check kubelet configuration for --container-runtime=docker or absence of --container-runtime-endpoint
Verify container runtime on nodes: kubectl get nodes -o wide (check CONTAINER-RUNTIME column)
Migrate to containerd, CRI-O, or install cri-dockerd before upgrading to 1.24+
Follow migration guide: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/migrating-from-dockershim/
Test workloads with new runtime before production upgrade

risk_paths.path_name: Kubeadm generates separate super-admin.conf with system:masters binding
risk_paths.description: Kubeadm 1.29 generates a separate super-admin.conf file. The admin.conf user is now bound to kubeadm:cluster-admins group (with cluster-admin role) instead of system:masters. Existing automation or procedures expecting admin.conf to have system:masters privileges will fail.

conditions.statement: Target Kubernetes version is 1.29 or higher

evidence.quote_or_summary: kubeadm: a separate "super-admin.conf" file is now deployed. The User in admin.conf is now bound to a new RBAC Group kubeadm:cluster-admins that has cluster-admin ClusterRole access. The User in super-admin.conf is now bound to the system:masters built-in super-powers / break-glass Group
evidence.relevance: Describes the new admin.conf vs super-admin.conf separation

conditions.statement: Deployment or automation relies on admin.conf having system:masters privileges

evidence.quote_or_summary: Before this change, the default admin.conf was bound to system:masters Group, which was undesired.
evidence.relevance: Confirms previous behavior that is changing

suggested_actions: Review automation and procedures using /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf
Determine if system:masters privileges are truly needed, or if cluster-admin role suffices
If system:masters is required, update scripts to use super-admin.conf instead
Note that super-admin.conf will only be generated on control plane nodes upgraded/initialized with kubeadm 1.29+
Consider migrating away from system:masters usage as it bypasses RBAC

risk_paths.path_name: Legacy service account token auto-generation disabled by default
risk_paths.description: The LegacyServiceAccountTokenNoAutoGeneration feature is beta and enabled by default in 1.24. Secret API objects containing service account tokens are no longer auto-generated for every ServiceAccount. Applications expecting auto-generated secrets will fail.

conditions.statement: Target Kubernetes version is 1.24 or higher (upgrade to 1.29 includes this)

evidence.quote_or_summary: The LegacyServiceAccountTokenNoAutoGeneration feature gate is beta, and enabled by default. When enabled, Secret API objects containing service account tokens are no longer auto-generated for every ServiceAccount.
evidence.relevance: Confirms feature is enabled by default in 1.24

conditions.statement: Application expects auto-generated service account token secrets to exist

evidence.quote_or_summary: Use the TokenRequest API to acquire service account tokens, or if a non-expiring token is required, create a Secret API object for the token controller to populate

suggested_actions: Identify applications reading service account tokens from auto-generated secrets
Migrate to TokenRequest API for short-lived tokens
For non-expiring tokens, manually create Secret objects following guide: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/secret/#service-account-token-secrets
Search for code mounting serviceaccount secrets or reading from /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token that may be affected

risk_paths.description: The kube-scheduler component config kubescheduler.config.k8s.io/v1beta3 is removed in v1.29. Scheduler configuration files must be migrated to kubescheduler.config.k8s.io/v1.

conditions.statement: Target Kubernetes version is 1.29 or higher

evidence.quote_or_summary: kube-scheduler component config (KubeSchedulerConfiguration) kubescheduler.config.k8s.io/v1beta3 is removed in v1.29. Migrated kube-scheduler configuration files to kubescheduler.config.k8s.io/v1.

conditions.statement: Kube-scheduler is configured with a v1beta3 configuration file

evidence.quote_or_summary: Migrated kube-scheduler configuration files to kubescheduler.config.k8s.io/v1.

suggested_actions: Check kube-scheduler configuration for --config flag and inspect referenced file
Grep scheduler config files for 'apiVersion: kubescheduler.config.k8s.io/v1beta3'
Migrate scheduler configuration to kubescheduler.config.k8s.io/v1 before upgrading to 1.29

risk_paths.path_name: Kubeadm upgrade no longer accepts component config for kube-proxy and kubelet
risk_paths.description: Kubeadm upgrade plan --config no longer accepts component configuration for kube-proxy and kubelet. This legacy behavior has been removed. Upgrade procedures passing these configs will fail.

conditions.statement: Target Kubernetes version is 1.29 or higher

evidence.quote_or_summary: Stopped accepting component configuration for kube-proxy and kubelet during kubeadm upgrade plan --config. This was a legacy behavior that was not well supported for upgrades
evidence.relevance: Confirms behavior change in upgrade command

conditions.statement: Kubeadm upgrade procedures pass kube-proxy or kubelet component config via --config

evidence.quote_or_summary: In the future, kubeadm will attempt alternative component config migration approaches.
evidence.relevance: Indicates this functionality is being removed

suggested_actions: Review kubeadm upgrade scripts and procedures
Remove kube-proxy and kubelet component configuration from kubeadm upgrade plan --config invocations
Manage component configuration separately from kubeadm upgrade process

open_questions: This report is based exclusively on official Kubernetes deprecation notices and changelogs; it has not analyzed the target application's actual manifests, code, or cluster configuration to determine which deprecated APIs are actively used
The runtime environment (current container runtime, service account token usage patterns, PSP deployment) has not been inspected—actual risk severity depends on whether these features are in use
Custom controllers or operators may use deprecated APIs internally even if application manifests are clean
The kubeadm-specific risks assume kubeadm is used for cluster management; clusters using other tools (kops, kubespray, managed services) may have different operational impacts
